summary:
NEVORA is an innovative project designed to address the challenge of wildfires using NASA satellite data, particularly the FIRMS system, to monitor fire locations, analyze thermal activity, and display fire information through an interactive map.
We developed a smart application that provides real-time fire monitoring data, including fire locations, detection times, thermal intensity, and analytical insights. It also presents alerts and indicators to help users understand wildfire activity and identify potentially high-risk areas.
NEVORA addresses the challenge by transforming complex satellite data into clear, accessible information that supports early fire detection, monitoring, and better decision-making for relevant authorities.
The importance of NEVORA lies in using space technology and artificial intelligence to protect lives, preserve the environment, reduce economic and environmental damage, and contribute to a safer and more sustainable future.
details: NEVORA is a web-based fire intelligence platform developed to make NASA satellite fire observations easier to understand, explore, and interpret. Our project focuses on improving how wildfire information is presented by bringing important data, such as location, observation time, satellite information, and fire-related measurements, into one organized experience. Wildfires can threaten communities, ecosystems, infrastructure, and air quality. Although satellite technology provides valuable information about active fires, understanding and comparing large amounts of data can be challenging. NEVORA aims to make this information clearer and more accessible through a simple and interactive platform. Our application is designed around NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System), which provides active fire observations from satellites such as VIIRS and MODIS. The data includes geographical coordinates, acquisition dates and times, satellite instruments, confidence levels, and Fire Radiative Power (FRP) when available. Our workflow focuses on organizing these observations, examining their attributes, and presenting them in a structured way. We developed our web application prototype using Base44, an AI-powered application development platform. We also used NASA FIRMS and NASA Earthdata as our main scientific data resources. Our development approach combines data organization, filtering concepts, API-based access planning, and an accessible web interface. The exact programming languages and underlying technologies are determined by the platform's generated implementation. What makes NEVORA different is its focus on connecting fire locations, observation times, and satellite attributes rather than presenting detections as isolated points. We considered data accuracy, clarity, usability, accessibility, and the importance of preserving original NASA data values. We also designed the project with future development and additional analysis in mind. NEVORA could benefit researchers, environmental analysts, fire-monitoring organizations, emergency planners, and communities by helping them explore satellite observations more easily. Its intended impact is to support better understanding of wildfire activity and provide a clearer starting point for informed environmental decisions. Our current achievement is a functional web application prototype and an organized NASA data workflow. Future development includes verified live NASA FIRMS integration, connected interactive mapping and filters, automated historical analysis, improved data-quality indicators, and broader user testing. NEVORA represents our belief that scientific data becomes more valuable when it is transformed into information that people can understand and use. Our goal is not simply to display fire data, but to make it more meaningful, accessible, and useful.
